sentences.text: This Criminal Appeal is filed seeking to set aside the judgment of conviction and sentence passed in SC No.106 of 2013, dated 30/09/2021 by the Mahalir Fast Track Court, Theni.
2.The case of the prosecution is that the accused and the victim girl loved each other for some-time.
They used to fix a particular place and had sexual intercourse for some-time.
The problem has arisen, when the victim girl asked the accused to marry her.
But the accused refused to marry her.

On the basis of the complaint given by the victim girl, a case in Crime No.341 of 2021 was registered by the 1st respondent police for the offences punishable under sections 417, 376 and 506(i) IPC and section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.

sentences.text: following charges were framed against the accused:-
( 1)The

victim girl was studying BA II Year in Hagi Kartha Rowther College,
Uthamapalayam during the relevant time; The accused was her neighbour working in Indian Army; When she was studying I year Course, she become friend with the accused;
She was taken to a park nearby in Bodi Mettu Road; On the false of marriage, she was subjected to sexual intercourse and thereby, the accused committed the offence punishable under section 376 IPC;
(2)In pursuance of the above said occurrence, when the victim girl demanded marriage, the accused told her that after performance of his sister's marriage, he will marry her.
By promising the same, she was subjected to sexual intercourse for several times, cheated the victim girl and thereby the accused committed the offence under section 417 IPC:

(3)In pursuance of the above said occurrence, when the parents of the victim girl asked the accused to marry her daughter, they were threatened by the accused with dire consequence and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis thereby, the accused committed the offence under section 506(i) IPC; and (4)Subsequent to the above said occurrence, the accused started abusing the victim girl and even went to the extent of committing criminal intimation to commit suicide and he will not marry her and thereby, the accused committed the offence under section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.
4.To that charges, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

2 5.During trial, on the side of the prosecution, 14 witnesses were examined and 4 documents exhibited.
On the side of the accused, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.
6.PW1 is the victim girl.

She was studying BA II year in Hagi Kartha Rowther College,
Uthamapalayam during the relevant time.
The accused was her neighbour working in Indian Army.
When she was studying I year Course, she become friend with the accused.
Later, they developed intimacy.
She was taken to a park nearby to Bodi Mettu Road.
He promised to marry her after the performance of his https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis sister's marriage.
By promising the same, she was subjected to sexual intercourse.
That sort of physical relationship continued for several years.
She started demanding marriage.
After that, the conduct of the accused started changing, started abusing her and even went to the extent of committing criminal intimation to commit suicide stating he will not marry her.
That relationship came to the knowledge of the family.
It started the problem.
In spite of the request made by her, the accused did not accept the marriage.

So, she lodged a complaint under Ex.A1.
7.The
complaint was received by PW12, who was working as Sub Inspector of Police in All Women Police Station, Theni,

on 29/12/2012, registered a case in Crime No.341 of 2012 for the offence under sections 417, 376 and 506(i) IPC and section 4 of TNPWH Act and submitted the original documents to the Court and copies to the concerned higher authorities.
8.Investigation was carried out by PW13, the Inspector of Police.
He recorded the statement of the witnesses, arrested the accused on 30/12/2012, took steps to send the victim girl and the accused for medical examination.
After the medical examination was over, he recorded the statement of the further witnesses and the Medical Officers.
After completing the investigation, filed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis a final report charging the accused for the offences under sections 417, 376 an 506(i) IPC and section 4 of TNPWH Act.
9.PW2 is the father of the victim girl namely PW1.
He remained hostile before the trial court.
He has stated that he was informed that the accused and the victim girl were secured by the police and went to the police station and he knows that PW1 lodged the complaint.
10.PW3 is the mother of the victim girl.
She corroborated PW1 with certain material particulars.
11.PW4 is the Sister-in-law of PW1.
She was informed that PW1 and the accused were loving each other and She has spoken about the compromise talk held in Jamath.
12.PW5 is the independent witness.
He turned hostile, so also PW6.
13.PW10 on the basis of the request made by the Investigating Officer, examined the accused and submitted a report stating that the accused is capable of performing sexual activities.

3 14.PW14
Medical Officer examined the victim girl on 03/01/2013 at the request made by the Investigating Officer and she found that hymen was not intact.
But no external injuries were found in her part parts.
She submitted a report under Ex.P4 I.e., Medical Report of the victim girl.
With that, the prosecution side evidence was closed.

15.The accused was questioned under section 313(1)
(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code about the incriminating circumstances against him.
He denied the evidence of the witnesses as false and stated that a false case has been foisted.
No witness was examined on the defence side.

16.At the conclusion of the trial process, the trial court held the accused guilty for the offence under section 417 IPC, sentenced him to undergo one year simple imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.3,000/-, in default to undergo 2 months simple imprisonment and acquitted the accused from the charges under section 376, 506(i)IPC and section 4 of the TNPHW Act.
17.Against the judgment of conviction and sentence, this criminal appeal is preferred by the accused.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
18.Heard both sides.
19.When the matter was taken up for hearing, a memo of compromise was filed by the parties.
The accused as well as the victim girl were present before this court.
The victim girl admitted that she got married, got two childrens living with her husband peacefully.
The appellant herein is now working in Indian Army and the fact of the pendency of the criminal case was intimated to the higher authorities.
Now, compromise has been reached by which the victim girl has no objection to acquit the appellant herein by setting aside the judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court.
20.Reading of the judgment of the trial court shows that it was not the forcible rape committed by the appellant upon the victim girl.
It was consensual in nature.
But however, promise was made by the appellant herein to marry the victim girl.
But what went wrong between them after some-time is not clear on record.
But however, the victim girl herself came forward to make a compromise since she settled the issue with the appellant herein.

21.So I am of the considered view that the confirmation of conviction and sentence may not be in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis interest of both, considering the above said acceptance and compromise reached between the parties.
22.In view of that
, this criminal appeal is allowed.
The judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court in SC No.106 of 2013, dated 30/09/2021 is set aside.
The accused is acquitted from the charge levelled against him.
The bail bond if any, executed by the accused shall stand discharged.
The fine amount if any paid by the accused shall be refunded to him.
The compromise memo, dated 29/08/2024 shall form part of the judgment.
